**Running Bash Action**

I’m ready to call functions.bash_action with the full and carefully constructed script. I’ll keep it concise but accurate, ensuring I handle potential edge cases. Even though journalctl could return large output, it’s manageable. I’ll be using grep instead of egrep for compatibility. {"script":"rm -rf cpu_check_workspace
mkdir cpu_check_workspace
cd cpu_check_workspace

# 2: capture CPU info
{ cat /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null || true; lscpu 2>/dev/null || true; echo "=== /sys/devices/system/cpu/possible ==="; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/possible 2>/dev/null || true; echo "=== /sys/devices/system/cpu/present ==="; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/present 2>/dev/null || true; } > cpuinfo_snapshot.txt

# 3: boot/kernel logs mentioning CPU enumeration
{ dmesg 2>/dev/null || true; journalctl -k 2>/dev/null || true; } | grep -E -i 'cpu|processor|smp|apic|microcode' 2>/dev/null > boot_logs.txt || true

# 4: virtualization/container indicators
{
  grep -i 'hypervisor' cpuinfo_snapshot.txt 2>/dev/null || true
  systemd-detect-virt -v 2>/dev/null || true
  [ -f /.dockerenv ] && echo "DOCKER_ENV" || true
  [ -f /run/.containerenv ] && echo "CONTAINER_ENV" || true
  [ -d /proc/xen ] && echo "XEN_PRESENT" || true
  grep -i 'container' cpuinfo_snapshot.txt 2>/dev/null || true
} > virtualization_flags.txt

# 5: extract processor identifier lines and record raw line count
grep -E '^processor' cpuinfo_snapshot.txt > raw_cpu_ids.txt || true
raw_count=$(wc -l < raw_cpu_ids.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
echo "$raw_count" > raw_cpu_count.txt

# 6: normalize entries (remove label and punctuation)
awk -F: '{ val=$2; gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", val); if (val!="") print val }' raw_cpu_ids.txt > normalized_cpu_ids.txt || true

# 7: deduplicate
sort -u normalized_cpu_ids.txt > unique_cpu_ids.txt || true
logical_count=$(wc -l < normalized_cpu_ids.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
unique_count=$(wc -l < unique_cpu_ids.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 0)

echo "logical_count=$logical_count" > cpu_counts.txt
echo "unique_count=$unique_count" >> cpu_counts.txt

# 8: cross-validate against boot_logs and virtualization flags
> cpu_validation_report.txt
while read -r id; do
  [ -z "$id" ] && continue
  if ! grep -E -q "\b(id|CPU|cpu|processor)[: =\[]*${id}\b" boot_logs.txt 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "ID_MISSING_IN_BOOT_LOGS: $id" >> cpu_validation_report.txt
  fi
done < unique_cpu_ids.txt

# Note virtualization effects
if grep -Ei -q 'hypervisor|docker|container|lxc|kvm|vmware|xen' virtualization_flags.txt 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "VIRTUALIZATION_INDICATORS_PRESENT:" >> cpu_validation_report.txt
  grep -Ei 'hypervisor|docker|container|lxc|kvm|vmware|xen' virtualization_flags.txt >> cpu_validation_report.txt 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# 9: summary
{
  echo "Validated logical CPU count: $logical_count"
  echo "Unique CPU identifiers: $unique_count"
  echo "See cpu_validation_report.txt for discrepancies and virtualization notes."
} > cpu_summary.txt

# Final output: print the number of CPUs (logical count)
echo "$logical_count" 
"}
